subject: Evidence sequencing and transfer controls onboarding for APAC pilot
messages:
From: Sana Rao <sana.rao@pacifichospital.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence & transfer controls for APAC pilot

Jordan / Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move forward with a small POC (clinical note summarization) across two hospitals in APAC. Before we can spin up test endpoints we need:

- A prioritized list of transfer-related evidence (SCCs, DTIA/TIA artifacts, subprocessor map, logging/retention statements).
- Clarity on sequencing: can we start with SCCs + contractual DPA and then add UK-specific IDTA/UK addendum only if UK data appears in scope?
- A short timeline for evidence delivery and any gaps that will block our procurement/legal team.

Attached is Pacific Health’s evidence request form (pacific_health_evidence_request_v1.pdf) with priority flags. Can you confirm what you can provide in the next 7–10 business days?

Thanks,
Sana Rao
Head of Partnerships
Pacific Health AI

Attachments: pacific_health_evidence_request_v1.pdf
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence & transfer controls for APAC pilot

Sana —

Thanks for the clear list. Internal plan below; Kimberly and Vivek I’m looping you for inputs and owners.

Quick answers first: yes, we can ship a prioritized evidence pack within the requested window for most items. There are a couple of things that may need a slightly longer lead time (third-party attestation for a subprocessor and detailed latency-based routing logs).

Proposed owners and asks:
- Kimberly: lead on contract sequencing and SCC/UK IDTA positioning; confirm whether we do SCCs as default with an optional UK addendum for UK-personal-data scenarios. Attach the control matrix you mentioned.
- Vivek: lead on subprocessor attestation and SRV logs; can you confirm what sampling we can provide for the KL1 subprocessor?
- Me: coordinate DocuSign package, procurement redlines, and demo environment access.

Next steps (this week):
1) Kimberly to send transfer-control matrix + recommended sequencing (SCC baseline, UK IDTA where applicable).
2) Vivek to confirm subprocessor evidence availability and any redaction rules.
3) I’ll prepare a short comms doc and DocuSign bundle for Pacific Health once we align.

I’ll also include Marissa on the legal comments once Kimberly posts the matrix.

—Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Evidence & transfer controls for APAC pilot

Jordan / team / Sana —

Attaching a draft transfer-control matrix that maps Pacific Health’s priority fields to what we can provide, the typical lead time, and a recommended sequencing. High level:

- Baseline: standard DPA + EU SCCs (we can apply SCCs contractually even if customer is APAC-first; it’s our baseline for international transfers).
- UK-specific: add UK IDTA / UK addendum only if UK-personal-data is in scope; this is typically a short add-on but requires legal acceptance (1–3 business days after we route).
- TIA/DTIA artifacts: we can provide a TIA summary and sampling logs; full DTIA export (per-request) may take 7–10 business days depending on retention windows.

Matrix highlights (see attachment):
- Subprocessor map: available now; attestation for KL1 subprocessor will require a signed NDA with that subprocessor — estimate 5 business days.
- Logging/retention statements: standard doc available immediately; audited logs export is a 5–7 day operation.

I’ve attached transfer-control-matrix.xlsx (draft). My recommendation is: ship the SCC-backed DPA and control matrix this week, begin subprocessor attestation in parallel, and only pursue UK IDTA if Pacific Health confirms UK data scope.

Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Operations (Contracts)
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachments: transfer-control-matrix.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2026 13:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence & transfer controls for APAC pilot — legal notes

Team —

Reading Kimberly’s matrix: a few legal flags and a proposed approval path. Quick summary:

1) SCCs as contractual baseline: agreeable. We treat SCC insertion as our default for cross-border transfers where the customer does not require a bespoke UK addendum.
2) UK IDTA / UK addendum: required when UK-personal-data is identified. If Pacific Health confirms UK residency for any data subset, we should attach the UK addendum rather than re-negotiating SCC clauses. That addendum needs lead time of ~2 business days for our standard template once Pacific confirms scope.
3) DTIA vs. TIA: we will provide a TIA summary (controls, flow diagrams, risk assessment) within the 7–10 business day window. Full DTIA exports that include raw logs need an approved data request and may require redaction—allow up to 10 business days.
4) Subprocessor attestations: approve Vivek’s plan; if KL1 requires a third-party NDA we should get that started immediately.

I attached a short DPA summary (redwood_dpa_summary.docx) with clauses we typically surface in POCs (retention, routing, encryption at rest/in transit, and audit rights). Once Jordan prepares the DocuSign bundle I’ll review redlines. If Pacific Health needs an SLA exception for latency routing (APAC edge), ask them to provide the expected throughput so we can map to Dedicated capacity options.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_dpa_summary.docx
